Proposition
[Principal Curvatures and Local Shape] 1. ch8:8.24Let $M\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}$ be a hypersurface, let $p\in M$, and let $k_1,\ldots ,k_n$ be its principal curvatures at $p$ for a chosen unit normal. Some Euclidean isometry sends $p$ to $0$ and a neighborhood of $p$ in $M$ to a graph $x^{n+1}=f(x^1,\ldots ,x^n)$ with \begin{equation} f(x)=\frac12\left(k_1(x^1)^2+\cdots +k_n(x^n)^2\right)+O(|x|^3). \tag {8.24} \end{equation}

Proof

\sketch Translate and rotate so that $p=0$, $T_pM$ is the first-coordinate hyperplane, the selected normal is $\partial _{n+1}$, and the second fundamental form is diagonal with entries $k_1,\ldots ,k_n$. The implicit function theorem represents $M$ locally by $X(u)=(u^1,\ldots ,u^n,f(u))$, with $f(0)=0$ and $df(0)=0$. Formula (8.23) then gives

\[ \frac{\partial ^2f}{\partial x^i\partial x^j}(0)=h_{ij}(0). \]

Taylor’s theorem yields (8.24).

□

If a smooth ambient field $N=N^i\partial _i$ restricts to a unit normal along $M$, the Weingarten equation gives, for $X=X^j\partial _j\in TM$, \begin{equation} sX=-\overline\nabla _XN =-\sum _{i,j=1}^{n+1}X^j(\partial _jN^i)\partial _i. \tag {8.25} \end{equation} If $M$ is locally a regular level set of $F$, one may take \[ N=\frac{\operatorname {grad}F}{|\operatorname {grad}F|}. \]
